translations.translation: e)
And this is “And on the day of your rejoicing… and you shall sound with trumpets… I am the L-rd your G-d.”
“And you shall sound” refers to the sounding of the shofar,
for the mitzvah of the day
(Rosh Hashanah)
is with the shofar,
as it is stated in the Mishnah:
The shofar is prolonged and the trumpets are shortened, for the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar.
And through this, the matter of the trumpets is also drawn down and revealed,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are two halves of a form,
meaning that Israel are rooted in His very Essence (Atzmus) and they determine the will
(as above, regarding “Whom did He consult? The souls of the righteous”),
and from the determined will it is drawn to the revealed will, etc., until it is drawn down below in this world,
and this is the main point.
That is, the drawing down through all the levels—
delight, will, intellect, emotions, and kingship, etc.—is an intermediary through which it is then drawn down into this world.
And as explained in the holy Tanya,
that in the entire order of the chain of descent, it is a descent from the light of His countenance,
and the ultimate intention is this lowly world, below which there is no lower,
a deep pit,
specifically in it
(in this lowly world)
was man created and in it was given the soul, literally a part of G-d from above,
and through his service in Torah and mitzvos
(“to work it and to guard it”)
the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is completed,
a dwelling place for His Essence and Being,
so that “these are the generations of Peretz, Peretz is written fully,”
which is higher even than it was at the beginning of creation, for “the world was created in its fullness,”
“Peretz begot… Dovid,”
Dovid, the King Messiah,
who will build the Holy Temple,
and it will be “and you shall sound with trumpets… before your G-d,”
“with trumpets and the sound of the shofar, shout before the King, the L-rd,”
literally
(in the Holy Temple)
below ten handbreadths.
For through the service during the time of exile, “sound the shofar at the new moon,”
“improve your deeds,”
and in a novel manner, as the precise wording of the verse “sound at the new moon a shofar”
(and not “sound a shofar at the new moon”),
as is known the explanation of the Baal Shem Tov
on this,
through this is brought about the matter of “make for yourself two trumpets… for summoning the congregation and for journeying of the camps,”
to gather all of Israel together and for journeying and proceeding from strength to strength,
from a deep pit to a high roof,
and the matter of “when
you go to war,” war with the animal soul,
and you will be saved through subjugation and transformation,
and through this it will be “and you shall sound with trumpets before your G-d” in the third Holy Temple, which will be built very soon by our righteous Messiah,
and all this in the manner of “and on the day of your rejoicing,”
and “everlasting joy upon their heads,”
speedily in our days, literally.
